newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Attorney says Avery, B.T. settle.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Attorney says Avery, B.T. settle.

text.p: U.S. Attorney Donald Stern said Thursday Avery Dennison Corp and B.T. Office Products International agreed to pay $375,000 to settle government civil charges against them.
The government charged the companies sold paper tags and correction tape to the General Services Administration which they knew, or should have known, did not fully meet its specifications.
Stern said the paper tags were used in government offices throughout the country to label boxes and other office items. The correction tape was used to correct typing errors.
The government said M.S. Ginn was the prime contractor under the contracts. It delegated its obligations to its subcontractor, Avery Dennison.
Subsequent to 1992, M.S. Ginn was acquired by B.T. Office Products through a merger. B.T. has agreed to pay Ginn's portion of the settlement.
The government said both parties cooperated fully with the investigation. It also said that in reaching this settlement, Avery Dennison and Ginn expressly denied the government's allegations.
